When these conflict with the documentation results above or with what you remember, prefer the most recent dated source.\\n\\n{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Uncover blind spots in AWS data plane operations with CloudTrail Event Coverage - AWS\",\"context\":\"AWS CloudTrail\\'s new feature, Event Coverage, allows users to view their data plane operations coverage at the account and organization levels in the AWS CloudTrail console. {"id": "57895c80-6ba7-468a-aefb-0952a05e09d8", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's what I found looking at your account's CloudTrail trails directly.

## Where your org trail coverage comes from

Your account currently sees **4 trails**, one of which is the organization trail:

| Trail | Scope | Owned by | What it logs |
|---|---|---|---|
| **JMERWIN_Org_Trail** (org trail) | Multi-region, all regions | Management account `012345678901_2` (home region us-east-2) | Global service events (IAM, etc.) + custom event selectors — this is the baseline applied to your account from the org |
| IsengardTrail-DO-NOT-DELETE | Multi-region | Your account `012345678901_1` | Management events only, no custom selectors — overlaps with the org trail's management-event coverage |
| nebula-data-events-trail | Single-region (us-east-1 only) | Your account | Custom event selectors — likely **data events** the org trail doesn't capture |
| nebula-single-region-trail | Single-region, no global events | Your account | Plain management events, one region only |

So the org trail is your **only multi-region source of global service events** (IAM, STS, etc.) and whatever data/management events its custom selectors define — and it's the piece you don't control locally, since it's defined and delivered to an S3 bucket in the management account. The three account-level trails layer on top of it, mostly adding redundant management-event coverage plus one trail (`nebula-data-events-trail`) that may be covering data events the org trail's selectors don't include. If you want to know exactly what the org trail's custom event selectors capture (data events, specific resource types), that configuration lives in the management account, not yours — this account only sees that it exists and is multi-region.

## Can auditors rely on Event history instead of a trail?

No — AWS's own documentation is explicit that Event history is **not a substitute for a trail** for audit purposes:

- **90-day retention only** — anything older simply isn't retrievable, trail or no trail.
- **Management events only** — no data events, no Insights events.
- **Per-region view** — it only shows activity for the region you're currently viewing, not an aggregated account/org view.
- Per the CloudTrail FAQ directly: *"For a complete record of account activity, including all management events, data events, and read-only activity, you must configure a CloudTrail trail."*

Your auditors need to go to the org trail (or an account-level trail / event data store) for anything beyond 90 days, for data events, or for a consolidated multi-region record — Event history is fine for quick lookups but isn't a durable or complete audit source.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
